title: Adaptive slab-slicing with jittered reclaim playbook for KV cache fragmentation and continuous-batching
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem:
Continuous request batching and variable-length KV entries are causing persistent micro-fragmentation in the GPU-resident KV cache. Short-lived prefixes from chat/batch tails create many tiny allocations that leave holes, degrading peak usable capacity and forcing frequent cold-model evictions. Existing slab/coalescing approaches reduce worst-case fragmentation but either increase tail latency (when compaction happens inline) or add CPU/GPU copy spikes during background defrag.

Proposal summary:
Introduce an adaptive slab-slicing allocator with workload-aware allocation tags and a jittered reclaim/playback strategy. The allocator carves slab pages into variable slices tuned per-model and per-tenant based on observed token-length distributions. Short-lived allocation classes (batch tails, short prefix reuse) map to micro-slices that are reclaimed aggressively with a randomized jitter window to avoid synchronized reclaim spikes across workers. Larger, long-lived allocations are placed into coarse slabs that prefer background relocation windows. Indirection (stable slot handles -> physical slice) is used to enable cheap pointer rehoming during compaction without blocking request fast-paths.

Key design elements:
- Adaptive slice profiles: each model/route has a small histogram of allocation sizes (5 buckets) maintained in shared telemetry. The allocator selects a slice profile that minimizes internal fragmentation for that workload.
- Allocation tags & TTL hints: request router attaches allocation hints (ephemeral|session|persistent) derived from batch metadata; allocator uses these hints to bias placement and eviction.
- Jittered reclaim windows: reclamation of micro-slices happens on per-GPU timers with randomized offsets to avoid correlated background work and batching-induced GC storms.
- Indirection table: stable 32-bit handles map to physical slice addresses; promotion/demotion during defrag updates the table atomically so in-flight KV lookups remain lock-free.
acceptance_criteria: No regression in 99th percentile generation latency under paced continuous batching (<= +2ms).
Measured fragmentation (wasted GPU bytes / total GPU resident) reduced by >= 30% for mixed short/long workload traces in staging benchmarks.
Background reclaim jitter prevents >20% simultaneous reclaim duty across GPUs in a pool during stress tests.
Feature gated behind runtime flag and opt-in per-tenant; rollout plan validated via canary with monitoring dashboards.
Unit tests for allocator invariants and integration tests covering handle promotion without request failures.

benchmarks: Throughput sweep: 1k -> 50k tokens/sec per GPU, measure mem-watermark and remap ops
Latency tail: 99/995/999 under continuous batching with 100ms batching window
risks_and_mitigation: Increased CPU overhead for indirection maintenance — mitigate by batching remaps and offloading to a low-priority worker thread.
Handle table growth under pathological workloads — cap entries per-GPU and fallback to coarse-slab path.
If jittered reclaim still correlates under synchronized load spikes, add adaptive backoff that spaces reclaim windows by observed reclaim latency.
Potential latency spikes during large background relocations — bound relocation byte-rate and throttle by observed token latency SLOs.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind runtime-flag: kv.adaptive_slicing = off by default.
Canary: enable on 1 dedicated GPU pool with synthetic mixed traces for 48h.
Monitor fragmentation and latency dashboards; if stable, expand to 10% of customer traffic over 7 days.
If regressions observed, rollback flag and run debug traces; follow failure mode runbook.
Full rollout tied to runtime-2.3 release after performance signoff.
